decisions.choice: Encode a deterministic store-plus-attempt invoice reference into Authorize.net invoiceNumber and refId within the 20-character limit: 8-hex SHA-256 store tag, a single '.', then the Commerce attempt id (max 11 chars). Characters are limited to Authorize.net-safe [A-Za-z0-9._-]. Creation fails closed on overflow or invalid chars (never truncate). After HMAC-SHA512 verification, receiveAuthorizeNetWebhook parses the reference and rejects (no transactionId write, no wake/alarm, no paid lookup) when the store tag does not match the URL siteId and the stored attempt site. Malformed or legacy bare attempt ids are rejected with no writes. A signed webhook still never marks paid; only authoritative getTransactionDetails lookup does.

The key is never sent to Payments or shown on a page. (3) The DinkusKit sign-in (Connect / Sign in again) is needed only for actions that change Stripe (Set up or resume Stripe, provider identity, recovery); pressing one with a lapsed sign-in shows the current status and asks to Sign in again. Status never asks for it. (4) A fresh pass is traded each load; no pass is kept. (5) Real problems are named: no key pasted says to paste it (with the last checked status when this admin has one); DinkusKit.com refusals use Ship's wording (unknown key, another store's key, Payments not connected for the store, cut off, suspended, busy); only Payments not connected offers Sign in again. decisions.choice: Yes. Payments works with or without Commerce. Two setup choices, in the same Payments plugin: (a) Connect, through the hosted payments.dinkuskit.com (Stripe Connect onboarding, store-account bindings, hosted checkout, verified webhooks); (b) the owner's own Stripe key (and Authorize.net keys), kept in the plugin's own secret settings, with the plugin talking straight to the provider and receiving the provider's signed webhook on its own public route, so no DinkusKit server is involved. On a Commerce store nothing changes: Commerce owns prices, checkout and the one order list, and payments.dinkuskit.com passes paid notices to Commerce because EmDash 1.2 Registry plugins cannot call each other; so choice (b) is offered only on sites without Commerce until a supported way for Commerce to hear 'paid' from a plugin exists. On a plain EmDash site Payments adds a Buy button that reads the price from the CMS on the server and keeps a small Sales list inside EmDash, with either choice; that Buy button and Sales list switch off when Commerce is connected. Payments may create the store's DinkusKit ID when Commerce is absent and Connect is used (dinkuskit store-connect-flow-081, store-connect-commerce-optional-085). Choice (b) adds provider hosts to the plugin's allowed hosts, which owners approve on upgrade; owners never paste a Stripe secret key into the hosted service. The charter line 'does not create a competing checkout or order model' is amended to allow that standalone Sales list only. Both choices are built together, after smokyclub.com is selling; checkout shape, cart, refunds display, snippet and docs are settled when the build is scoped.

decisions.choice: Keep both paid transactions recorded on the checkout (transactionIds, payments#95). Commerce makes one order from the first paid transaction. decisions.question: If one Authorize.net checkout ends up with two paid transactions, what does Payments do?
decisions.rationale: v1 scope is refunds by hand; automatic refunds risk refunding the wrong payment. Stripe cannot reach a second payment (one session per attempt, idempotency key, session_mismatch), so only Authorize.net needs this. Building a screen for a case the sandbox may show is unreachable would spend Payments bytes for nothing.

decisions.choice: Payments serves its own page at payments.dinkuskit.com/v1/pay/authorize-net/{siteId}/{sessionId} and returns it as the session's redirectUrl. The session Commerce sees never changes: for new sessions sessionId is a stable unguessable Payments id (attempt id plus 128 random bits), not the Authorize.net token, with the same redirectUrl, createdAt and expiresAt on every call, because Commerce refuses a changed session. Sessions already open keep their old token shape until they expire. When the shopper opens the page, Payments checks the checkout: paid, past expiresAt or unknown sends the shopper back to the store; otherwise it mints a fresh getHostedPaymentPageRequest token for the same attempt, amount and store-bound invoice reference and auto-submits it to Authorize.net by POST. The page takes no input, holds no card data (SAQ-A), never puts the token in a URL, and is not cached. Every try from any token carries the same invoice reference, so lookups, webhooks and the every-try-counts rule (payments#95) are unchanged; a shopper paying in two tabs at once falls under payments-authorize-net-paid-twice-044. Requests send duplicateWindow=0 so a declined shopper who fixes CVV or ZIP can retry at once. A checkout whose tries are all unpaid stays open (lookup returns open) until expiresAt; expired-unpaid is returned only once every try is unpaid and both expiresAt and the last minted token's 15-minute life plus a 5-minute margin have passed. Fraud holds (FDSPendingReview, FDSAuthorizedPendingReview) and any other unrecognized status stay unknown, never unpaid. Commerce does not change. Hosted Worker change only; deploy with --keep-vars on a quiet beta, on Ronald's go.
decisions.domain: Authorize.net hosted checkout page

Every try from any token carries the same invoice reference, so lookups, webhooks and the every-try-counts rule (payments#95) are unchanged; a shopper paying in two tabs at once falls under payments-authorize-net-paid-twice-044. Requests send duplicateWindow=0 so a declined shopper who fixes CVV or ZIP can retry at once. A checkout whose tries are all unpaid stays open (lookup returns open) until expiresAt; expired-unpaid is returned only once every try is unpaid and both expiresAt and the last minted token's 15-minute life plus a 5-minute margin have passed. Fraud holds (FDSPendingReview, FDSAuthorizedPendingReview) and any other unrecognized status stay unknown, never unpaid. Commerce does not change. Hosted Worker change only; deploy with --keep-vars on a quiet beta, on Ronald's go.

decisions.question: How does an Authorize.net shopper reach the card form for the whole 30-31 minute checkout window, when Authorize.net needs a POST and its form token lives only 15 minutes?
decisions.rationale: Authorize.net docs (developer.authorize.net Accept Hosted): the form is opened by an HTML POST of the token and the token is valid for 15 minutes. Minting on visit keeps Commerce's bounded 1800-1860 s window honest without changing the port. A Payments-owned page is the only place that can POST without Commerce knowing the provider. Re-minting makes a second paid try on one checkout more reachable, which 044 already handles by recording both and telling the owner to refund one by hand.

decisions.choice: Follow Stripe's recommended path: no Connect OAuth and no Accounts v1. Owners who already have Stripe use the existing 'Set up or resume Stripe' flow (Accounts v2 creation on 2026-09-30.endive plus Stripe-hosted account links), where Stripe's networked onboarding (on by default for the platform) lets the signed-in owner reuse an existing account's verified business details and bank. The store gets its own connected account under the same Stripe login, with its own balance and payment history; direct charges, the full Stripe Dashboard and Stripe fee/loss ownership are unchanged. Payment settings tells a store with no account: 'Already have Stripe? Sign in during setup to reuse your details.' No new routes, fields, states, secrets or Stripe settings; Accounts v1 support and OAuth stay off. The OAuth design in docs/existing-stripe-account-scope.md stays as research only.

decisions.rationale: Locked by Ronald 29 Oct 2026 23:40 UTC ('agreed'), replacing the 23:36 OAuth lock. Stripe: 'OAuth isn't recommended for new Connect platforms. We recommend using Connect Onboarding for Standard accounts' (docs/connect/oauth-standard-accounts); Accounts v2 limitations list OAuth as v1-only (docs/connect/accounts-v2); networked onboarding is enabled by default and works with Stripe-hosted onboarding when Stripe collects requirements (docs/connect/networked-onboarding), which matches our v2 accounts. Ronald prefers the upstream-recommended path. Trade-off accepted: a separate balance and history per store instead of attaching the exact existing account.

decisions.choice: Payment settings asks every Stripe store for a required Business country (where the business is registered) before Set up or resume Stripe, in TEST and LIVE alike, with no operator list or store cap. The choice is a select of Stripe's supported business countries; nothing is preselected and nothing is inferred (not from IP, hosting, currency, email, browser, Commerce store or shipping countries). Set up or resume Stripe sends the chosen ISO alpha-2 code to hosted POST /v1/connect, which validates it against the same list, saves it as the connection's creationCountry before the Accounts v2 create call and sends it as identity.country. Once saved, the country is fixed: the page shows it read-only and later setup presses reuse it, since Stripe does not let an account change country. A missing or unsupported country is refused before any Stripe call and creates nothing. Authorize.net is unchanged and never asks: its owner brings an existing merchant account whose country the acquirer already set. The operator-only TEST country bindings (STRIPE_TEST_MERCHANT_COUNTRY_SITES, STRIPE_TEST_MERCHANT_COUNTRY_CONFIG, their 16-store cap) and the one-time rejected-legacy-v2 preparation path tied to them are removed; no real stores exist yet, so no compatibility path is kept.

decisions.question: How does a store owner give Stripe the business country it requires before Payments creates the store's Stripe account, in TEST and LIVE, for every store?
decisions.rationale: Stripe Accounts v2 rejects account creation without identity.country (identity_country_required), and Payments had no source for it in LIVE and only an operator allowlist in TEST, which blocked independent stores (commerce#222). WooPayments asks for Business location on its payments settings page before onboarding and warns it cannot change later; Shopify takes it from the store's business address; Stripe-hosted onboarding fixes the country once set. Payments stays usable without Commerce, so it asks for the country itself instead of reading Commerce settings. Owner approved the shape, the supported-country list and removing the operator path on 2026-10-30.
